title: Climate of Hong Kong
claims: Hong Kong's climate is sub-tropical, tending towards temperate for nearly half the year.
January and February are cloudier, with occasional cold fronts followed by dry northerly winds, and it is not uncommon for temperatures to drop below 10°C in urban areas.
Sub-zero temperatures and frost also occur at times on high ground and in the New Territories.
January and December are usually the driest months in Hong Kong.
About 80 percent of Hong Kong's rain falls between May and September.
Mean annual rainfall ranges from about 1,400 mm at Ping Chau to more than 3,000 mm in the vicinity of Tai Mo Shan.
May to November are the months in which tropical cyclones of different intensities may strike Hong Kong, while July to September are the most likely months.
